subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should fresh Telegram setup switch to token-verified owner allowlist by default, while preserving explicit pairing-mode configs?
rationale: This changes the Telegram first-run authorization boundary and upgrade semantics, and automation cannot decide the product/security default without maintainer intent.

options.title: Token-verified allowlist default
options.body: Fresh setup generates a short token, captures only the matching sender ID, writes allowlist config, and keeps explicit pairing configs intact.

options.title: Keep pairing default
options.body: Pairing remains the fresh-install default and docs/setup continue guiding owners to manually configure allowlist when desired.

options.title: Post-bootstrap auto-flip only
options.body: First-run pairing remains unchanged, but a later owner-derived allowlist default is handled by the broader post-bootstrap policy work.

recommendation.title: Token-verified allowlist default
recommendation.body: Fresh setup generates a short token, captures only the matching sender ID, writes allowlist config, and keeps explicit pairing configs intact.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the broadest recent history across Telegram docs, runtime access, and config surfaces touched by this decision.
